rules.name: No-bid / sole-source / emergency procurement
rules.why: Purchases made without normal competitive bidding (sole source, emergency purchase, bid waiver, piggyback on another agency's contract) skip the usual price competition and deserve a look at the justification.

rules.name: After-the-fact approval / ratification
rules.why: Approving spending or contracts after the money was committed or the work was done bypasses the body's prior approval.

rules.name: Large contract increase / ceiling raise
rules.why: Amendments, change orders, or not-to-exceed increases that grow a contract by more than 25% can signal scope creep or an award that was underpriced to win.

rules.name: Possible bid splitting (amounts just under thresholds)
rules.why: The same vendor receiving several amounts just below common approval/bid thresholds ($25k, $50k, $100k) can indicate purchases split to avoid bidding or board approval.

rules.name: Vendor with many awards / large total
rules.why: Vendors appearing on many items or across several bodies, aggregated by name. Informational, for checking concentration of public money.

rules.name: Conflict of interest / recusal / related party
rules.why: Language about conflicts, recusals, related parties, or officials' employees and family members marks items where personal interests may be involved.

rules.name: Blank names or amounts
rules.why: Resolutions or appointments with blank names/amounts ("_____", TBD) are voted on before the public can see the key facts.

rules.name: Late additions, rule suspensions, repeated deferrals
rules.why: Walk-on items, suspension of rules, emergency ordinances, and items held over many times reduce public notice or signal contested items.

rules.name: Executive / closed session
rules.why: Closed sessions are limited under the Tennessee Open Meetings Act (generally attorney-client discussion of pending litigation). Sessions with no stated legal basis deserve a question.

rules.name: Settlements, severance, outside counsel, consultants, lobbyists
rules.why: Legal settlements, severance/separation payments, and hiring outside counsel, consultants or lobbyists are discretionary payments worth checking for amount and justification.

rules.name: Land deals: nominal price, below appraisal, eminent domain, PILOT/TIF
rules.why: Transfers of public property for nominal value or below appraisal, condemnations, land-bank transfers, and PILOT/TIF tax incentives move public value to private parties.

rules.name: Large dollar item on consent agenda
rules.why: Consent agendas are approved in one vote without discussion. Items over $1 million there get less scrutiny.

rules.name: Grants to nonprofits (check for ties to officials)
rules.why: Discretionary grants to nonprofits and community organizations should be checked manually for board or family ties to the officials sponsoring them.
